correctness.rationale: For n>=1, G_n is the reflexive undirected graph on all nonempty subsets of [n] with intersection adjacency. A surjective bounded morphism onto K_r^r is equivalent to a partition into r nonempty dominating fibers (forth automatic; back demands every vertex see each fiber). Complementary pairs {A,[n]\A}, with {empty,[n]} replaced by singleton {[n]}, yield 2^(n-1) dominating blocks. For an arbitrary induced subgraph W, Hall matching: a dominating singleton {A} has a private complement pair token because A^c cannot be in W; other blocks, of size at least two, touch >= one extra complement token per block, since tokens hold at most two W vertices. Hall gives r<=2^(n-1) for EVERY subcollection and hence every induced and generated subframe. For r_n=2^(n-1)+1 the K_r^r Jankov--Fine formula is frame-valid on all n-stage subframes. At n+1, complement partition yields 2^n dominating fibers and merging them gives r_n fibers, so bounded morphism onto K_r_n^r. Atomic coordinate truth values v(q_i)=[n+1]\{i} are available by source Lemma 5.2; q_i is true at B exactly when i is absent, so theta_A labels exactly B=A, and finite disjunctions label exactly fibers. Pullback of the standard diagram gives a falsifying translated valuation in stage n+1. Therefore strictness for all n including n=1. Independently reconstructed the assigned seven-file Git tree from authentic GitHub blob identifiers with exact SHA match. A separately coded exact induced-subgraph partition algorithm gave maxima 1,2,4 for n=1,2,3 (all 1,7,127 nonempty W); separately checked complement and fiber back conditions and coordinate coding through m=8. Finite tests are corroboration only, not the universal proof.

Hall matching supplies a sharp upper bound not immediately given by the full-graph min-degree argument. The propositional coordinate coding repairs an important restricted-atomic-valuation issue and may be reused in subsequent finite-stage calculations. The claim is not a narrow arbitrary parameter slice or known-table recomputation. It remains bounded: no complete axiomatizations, optimal separator complexity, or arbitrary infinite Boolean-algebra generalization.
